# shop-front

## Project overview

Storefront for a small bakery.

Users: Customers ordering on their phones.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Payments (handled by the provider's hosted page)

## Language policy

- Code, comments and commit messages: English.
- Docs: Italian.
- Replies to the user: Italian.

## Tech stack

Uses: TypeScript, Node.js, npm, Vitest.

- Use the Node.js version pinned in `.nvmrc` or in the `engines` field of package.json, never whatever version is installed globally. Why: Node.js versions differ in behavior and break native dependencies.
- Use npm for every install and script, and commit package-lock.json. Never run pnpm or yarn. Why: Mixing package managers creates conflicting lockfiles.

## Commands

- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Test: `npm test`

## Code style

- Keep `strict` enabled in tsconfig.json. Never use `any`; use `unknown` and narrow it. Why: Strict types catch errors at compile time, and `any` silently turns the checks off.
- App locales: it (default) and en. Write new text in the default locale only and mark it as untranslated in the others; human translators fill them in.

## Testing

- Run tests with `vitest run`; plain `vitest` starts watch mode in an interactive terminal and never exits. Put each test file next to the code it tests, named `*.test.ts` or `*.test.js`. Why: A watch-mode run blocks the shell until someone stops it.

## Safety rules

- Never edit, skip or delete an existing test to make it pass. Fix the code, or stop and ask. Why: A passing test suite is only meaningful if the tests stay honest.
